articles.headline: Clippers' Brandon Ingram gets in light work before practice
articles.description: Brandon Ingram, recovering from heel surgery, got in some light shooting and court work ahead of Clippers practice Tuesday in Hawai'i.
articles.body:
LA Clippers forward Brandon Ingram was out on the University of Hawai'i court for about 45 minutes prior to the team's first practice of training camp Tuesday morning, getting in some light shooting and court work as he continues to recover from heel surgery.

Ingram, then on the Toronto Raptors, missed the final two games of the first-round loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers last April. He had surgery in May and, during the procedure, doctors discovered and repaired a partially torn Achilles.

The Clippers were aware of the injury and elongated rehab timeline when they opted to execute the Kawhi Leonard trade for Ingram. Interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden said that a projected recovery is "about six months less" than a fully torn Achilles.

The Clippers are practicing at the University of Hawai'i all week before their preseason opener in Honolulu on Sunday afternoon against the Golden State Warriors.

Prior to the team's first workout, Ingram went through what appeared to be a half-speed shooting routine and some light defensive slides with assistant coach Jeff Van Gundy before testing the heel a bit more with some half-speed dribble moves.

Ingram has been ruled out to open the regular season but head coach Ty Lue said the timeline for his return remains vague. When the team started the contact portion of practice, Ingram watched from the side. 

"As he gets closer, we got to start getting him on the floor and going through the plays, seeing what he likes," Lue said.

articles.headline: Titans' Cam Ward on fans' threats to family: 'People are weird'
articles.description: Titans quarterback Cam Ward on Wednesday addressed fans' threats to his family on social media.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- The disappointment from the Tennessee Titans' 0-3 start to the season is mounting to the point where fans have started to send threatening messages to quarterback Cam Ward's family.

Ward spoke about the issue for the first time since his sister, Chantel Ward, took to social media earlier this week, saying she's tired of the threats.

"I mean, at the end of the day, people are weird," Cam Ward said Wednesday. "They can say whatever they want at the end of the day, but I think football will take care of a lot of it. My family knows the position I'm in and what I've wanted my whole life. They're in this position as well with me."

The disappointment hit a climax after Ward's interception at the end of the Titans' 12-7 loss to the New York Giants on Sunday. Tennessee had the ball on the Giants' seven-yard line with 24 seconds left in the game, but Ward's pass was intercepted by Giants' safety Jevon Holland.

Chantel Ward posted the following on social media soon after the game.

"The fact I even have to post this is diabolical," she wrote. "People see the football games, they see the wins, the losses, the interceptions, the touchdowns, the press conferences and everything that happens on the field. What they don't see is what comes with it for the people who love these players when the game is over.

"Criticize the game, criticize a play, be frustrated with your team. That's sports, and I completely understand that. But seeking out a player's sister, parents or other family members to personally attack them because you're upset about what happened on a football field is something completely different."

Some of the people in Cam Ward's circle have recently made posts in response to the fans complaining about the second-year quarterback's struggles. Fans have accused Ward's father, Calvin Ward, of sending messages as well.

Cam Ward said Wednesday that "there's also an aspect of me being someone's son or brother" in response to his family coming to his defense.

He said he believes winning will solve everything.

"Every adverse situation I have, I'm going to take on. It's really just about making plays on the football field. If I do that, we do that as a team, it's going to cut all that out."

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Ajay Mitchell, Ayo Dosunmu and other top sleepers to target
articles.description: Jim McCormick highlights the lesser known players who could be worth taking a flyer on in the final rounds of your fantasy draft.
articles.body:
After yet another seemingly endless NBA offseason, one that filled podcasts and social media feeds with content from the Finals through training camp, it can feel like we're overloaded with NBA information.

With fantasy drafters sharper than ever, do sleepers still exist?

Yes, yes they do. But finding them -- those players who are underrated and undervalued -- has become more challenging. This doesn't mean we can't or shouldn't try to hunt for value each and every new season.

It's a blend of timing, talent, circumstance, luck and flat-out waiver-wire magic that combines to keep this concept evergreen.

If sleepers were truly extinct, it would be difficult to explain how Ryan Rollins, who went undrafted in most leagues last season, finished ahead of stars such as Devin Booker and Keyonte George on the ESPN Player Rater, thanks to a rewarding creation role in a Milwaukee Bucks offense that leaned on him far more than anyone expected. It appears nearly everyone, save for maybe Doc Rivers, slept on Rollins last season.

In addition to leveraging the potential gems listed below, be sure to also check out our staff's roundtable on sleepers, breakouts and busts, which canvasses several strong sleepers, including my selection of the Orlando Magic's Anthony Black.

For the following list of notable sleepers, the focus is only on players found outside of the top 100 picks on average in ESPN live draft trends.

 Ajay Mitchell, PG/SG, Oklahoma City Thunder

A Most Improved candidate after a breakout second season as a playmaker in Oklahoma City, this 2024 second-round pick out of Belgium leapt from fringe role player to potential core building block in a single year. The runway is cleared for another takeoff for Mitchell; the team's tighter cap sheet led to some talent shedding this summer, which could result in a more concentrated rotation for Mark Daigneault this season.

If the playoffs are the ultimate proving ground, Mitchell is now certified; he went from roughly eight minutes a night in the Thunder's 2024-25 title run to 28.8 in 2025-26. In just over 100 playoff minutes without Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the floor, he averaged 26.5 points and 7.8 assists per 75 possessions. In a drubbing of the Los Angeles Lakers, Mitchell became the first player in Oklahoma City franchise history to post at least 20 points and 10 assists with zero turnovers in a playoff game. Don't leave drafts without him.

Zach Edey, C, Memphis Grizzlies

Availability is the entire question, although the risk appears to be baked into his draft position. Though he played just 11 games last season, Edey's elite production and evident growth as a player was undeniable. Emerging as one of the league's best interior scorers and rim protectors in an era that now celebrates size and its role in winning possessions, Edey and Cameron Boozer could become the next Marc Gasol and Zach Randolph of this new "Grit and Grind" formula.

Peyton Watson, SF/PF, Cleveland Cavaliers

For the latest odds on these and all other player props, visit DraftKings. 

*Implied odds convert the probability of an outcome projected by Mike Clay into a moneyline. Look for implied odds that are higher than the moneyline offered. For example if the implied odds are -150 and the moneyline is -110, then Clay's projection system indicates an advantage for the bettor. articles.headline: NFL survivor power rankings: Why you should use Vikings, Seahawks
articles.description: ESPN NFL survivor pool strategy, predictions and picks for Week 4 including the Vikings and Seahawks.
articles.body:
In many ways, this seems like the easiest ESPN NFL Survivor week of the year thus far. The two worst teams in the NFL on paper are on the road against quality teams. The 0-3 Tennessee Titans visit the 2-1 Baltimore Ravens, while the winless Miami Dolphins face the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.

The only problem? Both of those teams are on pace to be at least 30% selected on ESPN, meaning there is significant value in fading them in the event they lose this week.

However, the only other teams favored by at least four points this week are the Buffalo Bills and Seattle Seahawks, two of the top five Super Bowl favorites, both of whom have significant future value while having lower win probability this week. Plus, as bad as their opponents have looked this season, it's hard to see the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Chargers struggling this much the rest of the season.

Objectively, the Vikings are the best play when you combine win equity and future value. While the Vikings have some usable games down the road, hosting the Indianapolis Colts, Atlanta Falcons, Carolina Panthers and Washington Commanders, home games against the Dolphins are the most valuable to target in Survivor.

As of Wednesday morning, the Vikings are on pace to have lower selection than the Ravens on ESPN, making them the clear top pick this week in single-entry groups on ESPN. However, in higher-stakes pools, I expect the Vikings to be significantly more popular, making the decision more difficult.

If you want to avoid the chalk, the Seahawks are a strong consideration. They are on track to be less than 5% selected, and while they are projected to be favored in 11 of their last 14 games, the only obvious weeks to use them are Week 9 (vs. Arizona Cardinals) and Week 14 (vs. New York Giants).

If your primary goal is to not burn an elite team, the New Orleans Saints could fit the bill as home favorites against the Falcons. However, the Saints have the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL, according to ESPN Analytics, so if they are good enough to use this week, they will be similar-sized favorites down the road.

As a result, I will eat the chalk again this week and take the Vikings as my top pick in ESPN Survivor. If I have multiple entries, I will strongly consider mixing in the Ravens and Seahawks, and perhaps even the Packers and Bills. But in an 18-week season, there is plenty of time to get unique later in the year.

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Future value based on Mike Clay's cheat sheet. 

1. Minnesota Vikings (vs. Dolphins)

The Vikings are the best combination of win equity and lack of future value. The Dolphins grade as the worst team in the NFL according to ESPN Analytics, so every time they are on the road, their opponent is a strong consideration. If the Vikings start to trend toward being 50% selected, I will strongly consider pivoting to the Ravens or Seahawks, but at under 40%, they are the top pick this week on ESPN.

Chance to win: 8

articles.headline: Chiefs LT Simmons recovering from bulging disk, Reid says
articles.description: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said on Wednesday that left tackle Josh Simmons, who has not practiced with his teammates since Aug. 17, is recovering from a bulging disc.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons, the 2025 first-round pick, has not practiced with his teammates since Aug. 17, when he sustained a lower back injury. After six weeks without details on the severity of the injury, coach Andy Reid revealed Wednesday that Simmons is recovering from a bulging disk.

"It's kind of hindered the strength of his leg, but he's working through it," Reid said of Simmons. "He's working through it. He's here every day, grinding away. We didn't have to make any roster moves or have to put him on [injured reserve]. It's all worked out."

Simmons didn't participate in Wednesday's practice, and he's not expected to play Sunday when the Chiefs face the Las Vegas Raiders. Reid, though, acknowledged that the Chiefs believe Simmons will avoid needed surgery to repair his lower back.

"The positive is he's making progress and getting stronger, which is important," Reid said. "We all know backs can be a little tricky. You never know [the return-to-play timeline] with these things. The exams that he's had [have shown] he's making progress, which is the biggest positive of everything.

"I think we're heading in the right direction here. Knock on wood, we're going to be in a good place here with [more] time."

Since selecting Simmons in the draft, the Chiefs have played more games without him (12) than with him (eight).

He missed a four-game stretch last season when he left the Chiefs hours before kickoff against the Detroit Lions to fly back to his hometown of San Diego for what the team called a "family situation." Simmons returned and played well, but he sustained a season-ending injury when he dislocated and fractured his left wrist in a loss on Thanksgiving Day against the Dallas Cowboys. The injury occurred when he collided with former running back Kareem Hunt, who was attempting a chip-block on defensive end Jadeveon Clowney.

This season, the Chiefs have had Kahlil Benson, an undrafted rookie from Indiana, start in Simmons' absence. Although the Chiefs defeated the Miami Dolphins this past Sunday to move to 3-0, Benson struggled at times in one-on-one matchups against defensive ends Josh Uche and Chop Robinson. The Dolphins hit Mahomes a season-high five times.

The Chiefs are hopeful that Simmons can return to the lineup after their bye week to play Oct. 18 against the Los Angeles Chargers.

When on the field last season, Simmons allowed a pressure rate of just 6.6%, the third-lowest mark among left tackles and the second lowest by a rookie left tackle since 2018 (minimum 150 pass blocks), according to Next Gen Stats.

"You put in the work every single day and you want to get back and be back on that field," Mahomes said of Simmons. "I've been seeing him and he's putting in the work, whatever it takes to get on the field as quickly as possible. Hopefully that's a little quicker rather than later.

"I'm excited for him, man. He's competing and he's doing whatever he can to be back out there."

articles.headline: Michael Jordan's Game 3 'Last Dance' jersey sold for record amount
articles.description: Jordan wore the jersey in Game 3 of the 1998 NBA Finals.
articles.body:
A highly valued piece from the Chicago Bulls' "Last Dance" run has sold for a record price.

Michael Jordan's game-worn jersey from Game 3 of the 1998 NBA Finals was auctioned Tuesday for a record-breaking $12,260,000. It was sold by Rob Gough via Joopiter, a digital marketplace and auction house curated by Pharrell Williams. 

It was projected to sell between $10 million to $15 million and received one bid before closing, according to The Athletic.

The auction closed at 8:06 p.m. EST, with the final price marking a new record for an NBA jersey sale -- the previous being Jordan's Game 1 jersey from the same 1998 series in September 2022 at $10.1 million at Sotheby's. 

Jordan's jersey was registered in August, was authenticated by MeiGray in December 2015, and was photo-matched to two specific photos from Getty Images.

The jersey was in possession Gough, who purchased the jersey in 2023 according to Sportico.  Before Gough, Bill Thoma of Chicago possessed the jersey, according to a March 2015 letter posted on Joopiter. In the letter, he wrote he purchased the jersey from Evan LaManna, a sales manager and partner in Upper Class Collectibles in New Jersey. At the time the letter was written, Thoma says the jersey transaction was completed "about 8 or 9 years ago."

He also expressed that LaManna had a professional relationship with Jordan and obtained the jersey from a "close associate" of the Bulls legend.

The jersey features an NBA Finals logo patch at the top right chest, mesh material and an NBA Authentics tag with the size 50 tag at the bottom left of the jersey.

In that particular game, Jordan finished with 24 points, three rebounds and two assists in a 96-54 blowout to help Chicago advance to a 2-1 lead over the Utah Jazz. The Bulls won the 1998 Finals in six games, and Jordan announced his second retirement on Jan. 13, 1999. He finished his NBA career with six championships.

articles.headline: Erling Haaland unaffected by Man City guilty verdict, says Norway teammate
articles.description: Norway defender Kristoffer Ajer said football's "biggest star" Erling Haaland has been unaffected by Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.
articles.body:
Norway defender Kristoffer Ajer said football's "biggest star" Erling Haaland has been unaffected by Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

Haaland will play for the first time on Thursday since an independent panel's verdict released on Tuesday said that City arranged "sham" contracts with commercial partners to artificially inflate their commercial earnings, filed "misstated" accounts to conceal the true nature of their finances and "significantly" breached Premier League and UEFA spending limits.

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Pep after City verdict: 'I am behind my club'

- Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Guardiola's legacy?

The Premier League said sanctions will be decided in a separate hearing held by the independent commission, while City have continued to deny the charges and say they will appeal the verdict.

Wales will host Norway in a Nations League fixture at Cardiff City Stadium, when Haaland will be in the spotlight and seeking to add to his extraordinary international record of 65 goals in 57 games.

"Ever since I met him brings lot of energy and joy to the group," Brentford center back Ajer said when asked about Haaland's demeanor in the Norway camp since City's guilty verdict was announced on Tuesday.

"That's the biggest compliment I always give, he hasn't changed a bit from the moment I met him, even though he's the the biggest star on the planet right now.

"He been exactly the same the last few days as well which is is not a surprise for me."

Reports of City's guilty verdict first surfaced in the media on Friday.

Haaland scored against Portugal in a 2-1 defeat two days later, after earlier scoring two versus Denmark to extend his record as the Nations League's all-time top scorer to 22.

Ajer said: "He's the best player in the world if you ask me, so hopefully he scores a few tomorrow as well.

"I have to admit that honestly I've read very little into it [the City situation]. We don't talk about it much here.

"Obviously, it was a statement released yesterday, so it's quite fresh and new. But we're just footballers, we don't know all the ins and outs and all the stuff that's being talked about in the media.

"So we haven't really had any fantastic discussions about it where we know a lot."

PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Ravens' Henry: 'Always love' for Titans, but not much this Sunday
articles.description: Ravens RB Derrick Henry faces his former team, the Titans, on Sunday for the first time since leaving Tennessee after the 2023 season. He said it's "always love" for the Titans, just not much when they play on Sunday.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry has been getting nonstop texts this week heading into Sunday's reunion with the Tennessee Titans.

"It's still like family there," Henry said Wednesday. "So it's always love, but it ain't going to be much love on Sunday, though."

Henry has tried to downplay his first game against his former team even though he is still regarded as one of the most dominant players in Titans history. During his eight seasons in Tennessee, he won two rushing titles (2019 and 2020) and was named NFL Offensive Player of the Year in 2020, leaving the Titans as the franchise's second all-time leading rusher behind Eddie George.

On Sunday, Henry becomes the fourth player to face a team that he produced at least 9,000 yards rushing and 90 rushing touchdowns for in his career. The others were: Emmitt Smith, who played the Dallas Cowboys in 2003; LaDainian Tomlinson, who played the Chargers in 2011 and Adrian Peterson, who played the Minnesota Vikings four times after leaving there.

"It's going to be a crazy moment to be playing against the team that I came in the league playing for," Henry said. "But I ain't trying to make too much of it, though."

Henry joined the Ravens in March 2024, signing a two-year, $16 million contract. Before Henry reached an agreement with Baltimore, the Titans had signed running back Tony Pollard to a three-year, $21.75 million deal.

On Wednesday, Henry said Tennessee made no attempt to keep him in free agency.

"They shipped me out," Henry initially said, before adding, "I don't want to say it like that. It's always love."

How did it make Henry feel to not receive an offer from the Titans?

"It was bittersweet," Henry said. "I think I knew the writing was on the wall throughout that season and they were ready to move on. Good things don't last forever. So it was time for me to find a new home and I knew what that home I wanted it to be and it was here."

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson said Henry's teammates are aware of the magnitude of this game.

"It not only means a lot to him but for us, too," Jackson said. "We want him to win versus those guys."

Since Henry joined Baltimore, he has produced 3,817 yards rushing and 38 rushing touchdowns -- both of which lead the NFL over that span. During that time, Pollard has totaled 2,334 yards rushing and 10 rushing touchdowns.

When he knew his time was over in Tennessee, Henry said the Ravens were at the top of his list when he hit free agency.

"I knew where I wanted to be." Henry said with a smile. "So definitely been happy over these last couple years."
